name: Haiming
kurzbeschreibung: Warm and welcoming community at the entrance to the Ötztal, featuring the Haiminger Badesee and a picturesque Inn-Radweg.
title: Haiming
metaDescription: Haiming at the gateway to the Ötztal: Tyrol's premier apple village, outdoor adventures at AREA 47, rafting, and climbing on the Geierwand.
beschreibung:
Overview

Haiming is situated at an elevation of 670 metres in the Tyrolean Upper Inn Valley in the district of Imst, strategically located right at the confluence of the Ötztaler Ache with the River Inn. The extensive municipality covers roughly 40 square kilometres and is home to around 4,800 residents. Sheltered beneath the striking Tschirgant massif, Haiming enjoys a remarkably mild microclimate. This favourable weather makes it North Tyrol's largest fruit-growing community, widely celebrated as Tyrol's traditional apple village. Simultaneously, with the world-renowned AREA 47 outdoor park and raging glacial rivers, Haiming stands as an international hub for whitewater and adventure sports.

History

Human settlement around Haiming stretches back thousands of years, as evidenced by bronze age urnfield burials dating to around 1200 BC. The first official documentary mention of the Tyrolean village occurred on February 19, 1269, when Count Meinhard II of Tyrol exchanged estates with Heinrich of Eschenlohe. For centuries, rural life centred on farming the fertile alluvial soils. The town underwent rapid development in 1883 with the opening of the Arlberg Railway, which fostered the vibrant district of Ötztal-Bahnhof. The architectural centerpiece of the main village is the parish church dedicated to Saints Chrysanthus and Daria, originally late-Gothic and later enhanced with elegant Baroque features.

Getting There

Thanks to its prime transport connections, Haiming is exceptionally easy to reach. By automobile, drivers take the Inntal Motorway A12 directly to the Haiming-Ötztal junction, or travel via the federal road B171. Train travellers benefit from the major railway hub at Ötztal station, an essential stop for ÖBB Railjet and regional express services on the transalpine Arlberg line. Both Ötztal and the central Haiming stop are served frequently by Tyrol S-Bahn lines S4 and S5. A dense local bus network links the railway stations directly to the village centre and the upper reaches of the Ötztal valley.

Tips

Thrill-seekers head to AREA 47, Austria's largest outdoor adventure park featuring a massive water area, extreme slides, a high-ropes course, and wakeboarding facilities. Whitewater enthusiasts embark on adrenaline-fueled rafting and canyoning tours through the famous Imst Gorge and the torrential Ötztaler Ache. Rock climbers will relish the challenging Geierwand via ferrata on the Tschirgant cliffs, boasting breathtaking aerial views across the Inn Valley. In autumn, food lovers should not miss the acclaimed Haiminger Markttage, North Tyrol's premier agricultural harvest market showcasing fresh apples, ciders, and regional delicacies.
